key_insight: The paper reframes online learning in non-stationary environments as Bayesian state tracking, but learns a compact latent representation so adaptation stays fast and tractable. This lets deep models update sequentially from streaming data without filtering over the full parameter space.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of adapting machine learning models to changing data streams while meeting strict computation limits. Existing Bayesian online learning methods are often too expensive for modern deep models or depend on overly restrictive approximations.
method: Cast online learning as sequential Bayesian filtering over model states.
Learn a low-dimensional latent space that captures parameter dynamics instead of tracking all weights directly.
Perform Bayesian updates in latent space to enable efficient online adaptation under non-stationarity.
impact: This makes principled online adaptation more practical for real-world ML systems that must learn continuously from streaming data. Practitioners gain a way to balance responsiveness, uncertainty awareness, and computational efficiency.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: streaming data -> latent Bayesian tracker -> updated model
Side-by-side comparison of full-parameter filtering vs latent-space tracking
Timeline chart showing model adaptation across distribution shifts
Icon set for non-stationarity, Bayesian update, and compute efficiency
paper_title: Online Learning via Learned Latent Bayesian Tracking
paper_authors: Guy Gerson, Tomer Raviv, Nir Shlezinger, Tirza Routtenberg, Osvaldo Simeone
